messages:

Subject: Packaging schematic + fallback options (Clearpoint)

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the demo last week. The leadership team wants a clear packaging option that lets us: (1) upgrade to higher throughput during product launches, (2) fall back to a cheaper model automatically when load subsides, and (3) keep certain premium features gated to avoid surprise costs.

Attached is a short spreadsheet with our desired traffic profile and a few baseline requirements (Clearpoint_Desired_State.xlsx). Can you confirm whether Redwood can:
- Provide a 90-day trial window for burst credits?
- Offer a staged upgrade path (small -> medium -> dedicated) with discounted anchoring for year-one?
- Guarantee automatic model-fallback and a documented SLA when we hit sustained load?

Also cc'ing procurement shortly so they can see the timeline. We're aiming to finalize packaging and commercial terms by early August.

Thanks,
Daniel Park
Head of Product
Clearpoint AI

--

Subject: Re: Packaging schematic + fallback options (Clearpoint)

Hi Daniel — really helpful detail, thanks for sending the traffic profile. High level answers below; I'll follow up with a short proposal (two options) and a calendar invite.

Short answers:
- 90-day trial for burst credits: Yes, we can pilot burst credits scoped to a monthly cap; finance will propose two tiered caps.
- Staged upgrade path: Yes — we typically recommend an "Elastic Bridge" (metered burst + prefix cache) for short-term launches and an "Anchored Reserve" (committed capacity with step-up credits) for predictable growth.
- Model fallback & SLA: We support automatic fallback to compatible model variants in the same family; SLA depends on whether you choose Hosted vs Dedicated. We'll document expected latencies and failover behaviors.

Next steps:
1) I'll prepare two packaging schematics (Elastic Bridge vs Anchored Reserve) with price bands and trial mechanics.
2) Ben — can you draft the two discount scaffolds we discussed (pilot-level and committed-year-one)?
3) Lauren — can you attach the MAD (mutual action plan) template and map to procurement milestones?

I'll aim to get the docs to you by tomorrow EOD. Meeting: propose Wed 7/22 10am PT — ok for you?

Best,
Vivek
VP, Partnerships & GTM
Redwood Inference

Vivek — draft discount scaffolds below; quick thoughts:

Pilot scaffold (90-day burst trial):
- 100k burst tokens included / month for 3 months
- 20% pilot discount on hosted per-token rates during pilot
- No long-term commitment required; transition credit of 15% applied to first 3 months of committed term if they convert within 30 days

Committed year-one scaffold (Anchored Reserve):
- 12-month commit with 20% baseline discount on committed units
- Step-up credit: when they add >25% capacity within first 6 months, provide additional 10% credit on incremental units for 3 months
- Feature bundling: include prefix caching + per-route tracing as part of the year-one bundle (value-add)

Notes on gating features: we should define which features are metered (e.g., per-token tooling like reranking/safety-eval runs) vs included (caching, basic tracing). Avoid gating core generation unless requested.

I'll take lead on pricing table and attach a short spreadsheet to the proposal.

—Ben
Director, Sales Ops
Redwood Inference

Hi Daniel — attaching the initial packaging schematic and a mutual action plan that maps to procurement milestones.

Attachments: packaging_schematic_v1.pdf, mutual_action_plan.docx (see cover sheet for timeline + responsibilities).

Short answers inline:
- Step-up credit applies forward from the month they cross the threshold; we can offer a one-time retroactive credit for the crossing month as a negotiation point (standard concession).
- Overflow protection add-on (hot-path routing): we can provide it during the pilot; pricing for overflow routing is metered at a higher per-token rate but can be capped. Proposed add-on: metered overflow at +30% per-token rate with a safety cap they can set.
- Redlines/lead time: procurement usually needs 7–10 business days for SOW review; legal prefers a single consolidated redline package.

Proposed next steps:
1) We lock the pilot cap and overflow cap in the MAD (I've filled conservative values; see attached).
2) Redwood sends a short SOW & pricing appendix for their procurement to review (we can provide a draft within 48 hours).
3) Schedule a 30-min working session Wed 7/22 10am PT to walk the schematic and MAD — we'll invite legal/procurement if they want.

Deal meta: DEAL-3482 (prelim).

Warmly,
Lauren Bishop
